cautions_and_proof_limits: The finite-population CLT is stated rather than proved in the inspected section; it is not inherited as a proved theorem. A nondegenerate normalized variance and a specified triangular-array condition would be essential.

A conservative asymptotic variance does not imply a realized estimate always exceeds true variance or exact finite-sample coverage. A limit at nominal coverage alone also does not establish eventual finite coverage above nominal.
Terminology for CRE in the later superpopulation section includes independent assignment. Our chapter distinguishes fixed treatment count from independent Bernoulli assignment.

cautions_and_proof_limits: An exposure label must map equal labels to equal potential outcomes across assignments; merely calculating a network label does not validate it.
Positive marginal exposure probabilities identify that target mean but do not guarantee all joint probabilities are positive or all contrast variance terms are observable.
General asymptotic inference, later refinements and empirical results are outside inspected/proved scope.

cautions_and_proof_limits: Power quantile expressions in this source are planning approximations. Our original known-Gaussian example derives both tails exactly; no unknown-variance exact t power is inherited.
Distinguish standard-error multiplier sqrt(1+(m-1)rho) from variance multiplier1+(m-1)rho; rho is the common-component share, not the idiosyncratic variance share.
Displayed group-count formula scales as inverse square root of J with critical values held fixed; the adjacent roughly proportional wording must not be copied literally.
Increasing compliance strengthens the assignment contrast under fixed local effect; its inverse enters a detectable local effect. Do not reverse that direction.
Basic bounded-outcome attrition intervals here are original population identification bounds, not the more restrictive monotonicity/rank-based trimming bounds discussed later in the source.
No historical application, general multiarm allocation claim or source exercise is adopted as our own evidence.

cautions: Random assignment of an encouragement does not itself exclude its direct outcome effect. Administrative-selection and historical application examples were read but are neither reproduced nor claimed to establish validity in a new case.

original_work: Seven finite or fully specified Gaussian teaching cases; all exercise prompts, solutions, numerical tables, counterexamples, analytic inversion, known-range bound, covariance certificates and retention examples are original. No empirical data or historical intervention finding is adopted.
runtime_policy: This record is one of four portable runtime author files. Preparation records, PDFs, canonical chapters/catalogue and the network are provenance only and are not required by the checker.
excluded_claims: A finite-population CLT from a finite variance formula
Pointwise domination or exact normal coverage from expected Neyman conservatism
Weak-average coverage from constant-effect sharp-null inversion
Generic unknown-variance, cluster, large-network or selection-adjusted inference
Exclusion, exposure-map sufficiency or missing at random from random assignment alone
Observed-law identification of all joint variance products when joint probabilities vanish
A population identification interval as a sampling confidence interval
Empirical effectiveness, transport or external human certification
